meta.prefilled_meaning: Two different things. (1) Enumeration forms: every SIR enumeration form is pre-printed by the Commission with the elector's name, EPIC number, address, part and photograph, and the elector adds a photograph, details and a signature (Bihar 'semi-filled' forms, Hyderabad DEO). Disputes about these are about who filled or uploaded them: BLOs uploading forms without voters (Bihar, ADR allegation), BLOs uploading blank backs (Serilingampally, BJP allegation), BLOs handing forms in bulk to AIMIM camps (Hyderabad, BJP allegation). (2) Form 7: in every state where the press describes a 'pre-printed' or 'pre-filled' Form 7, it means the part about the voter to be deleted (name, EPIC, address, booth) was printed in advance, and the objector's part was handwritten or left blank. Telangana: Musheerabad, Bahadurpura (Aliyabad) and Goshamahal, unsigned or with only the objector's name handwritten (Congress complaint, South First, Deccan Chronicle, FIR). Karnataka: Babaleshwar (The Hindu, already in process.json) and Belagavi (voter details filled, objector handwritten or blank). Gujarat Somnath: voter details printed in English, objector handwritten in Gujarati. Uttar Pradesh Shamli: printed with EPIC numbers. Assam Karimganj: 'half-printed and half-handwritten'. West Bengal Khatra: 'pre-filled' Form 7s seized in a vehicle, contents not described. Rajasthan: Congress alleges 'computerised' printed forms. No source found describes a party circulating blank pre-filled forms to voters for their own use.
meta.not_found: No Form 7 report specific to Charminar, Yakutpura, Malakpet, Chandrayangutta or Jubilee Hills. No Form 7 complaint by the BRS. The CEO Telangana memo of 5 October 2026 and the ECI clarification of January 2026 were found only as quoted in the press. No Maharashtra bulk Form 7 episode found (11,251 Form 7s statewide to 4 October per ThePrint).

items.headline: 50,000 Forms Filed Seeking Deletion of Votes
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Commission had received close to 50,000 Form 7 applications in Telangana after the draft roll, and that parties asked officials in Hyderabad for the Form 10 lists of objections by constituency.
items.quote: Amid nearly 93 lakh voters listed with logical discrepancies or placed in the absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) list, the Election Commission of India (ECI) has received close to 50,000 Form-7 applications seeking deletion of names or raising objections to entries in the draft electoral rolls. Political parties have asked election officials to provide details of the Form-7 applications through Form 10, which is the consolidated list of objections and deletion requests received through Form 7.
items.response: Deccan Chronicle reported that officials gave parties the total number of applications at a meeting at the GHMC office but did not share figures by Assembly constituency.

items.headline: Nearly 29,000 Form-7 applications filed during Telangana SIR
items.claim: Telangana Today reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, said 28,753 Form 7 applications had been filed in Telangana, about 5,000 of them in Hyderabad, and that forms received in bulk would be examined with special care.
items.quote: Revealing SIR of electoral rolls status in the State on Thursday, Telangana Chief Electoral Officer C Sudharsan Reddy said 28,753 Form-7 applications were filed, so far. “Special care is being taken while deciding the Form-7 received in bulk. All claims and objections will be placed on the website of the CEO, so that citizens are able to see the list and lodge objections, if any,” he said.

items.headline: Telangana SIR: Congress alleges vote deletion bid in Musheerabad
items.claim: Siasat reported that the Telangana Congress complained to the Chief Electoral Officer that a BJP booth agent in Musheerabad had filed about 30 Form 7 applications against a Congress booth agent and his family on forms that were printed in advance. This is the Congress's allegation.
items.quote: Kumar said that the applications were pre-printed and prepared in advance, rather than being individually and independently prepared by the concerned applicants. “The circumstances raise serious questions regarding the source from which these forms were obtained, who prepared them, who supplied the information contained in them, and whether the applications were submitted with the knowledge and consent of the persons shown as applicants.” the complaint stated.
items.response: Siasat reported that the Congress asked for an investigation rather than for the allegations to be presumed true, including a forensic examination of whether the forms came from a common source.

items.headline: After Musheerabad, Telangana Congress says it found more pre-printed Form 7s aimed at deleting Muslim voters in Bahadurpura
items.claim: The South First reported that it had seen a Form 7 from a polling station in Aliyabad, in Bahadurpura, with the voter's details printed and the objector's part left blank. The Congress alleged that such forms had been handed to BJP booth agents through the party's constituency in-charges.
items.quote: South First has seen one such pre-printed application seeking the deletion of a Muslim voter from a polling station in Aliyabad. It has the voter’s details and address pre-filled, but the applicant’s details are left blank.
items.response: The South First reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, said at a press briefing that officials would thoroughly verify all Form 7 applications before making any decision.

items.headline: SIR: 15-Pre-Printed Form 7 Now Appear in Goshamahal Constituency
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported, citing Congress sources, that a BJP booth agent brought 15 pre-printed Form 7s to the booth officer at booth 173 in Goshamahal and that the booth officer refused to accept them.
items.quote: Hyderabad: After Musheerabad and Bahadurpura Assembly constituencies, 15-pre-printed Form 7, seeking deletion of Muslim names from voter lists surfaced in Goshamahal constituency. The issue came to light after the local booth level officer (BLO) refused to accept the forms allegedly submitted by BJP booth level agent (BLA).
items.response: Deccan Chronicle reported that the District Election Officer had reportedly directed the Musheerabad ERO to file criminal cases against the booth agent there.

items.headline: Owaisi says Hyderabad will see massive protests if ECI doesn’t act on Form 7 misuse
items.claim: The News Minute reported that AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that Form 7s were being filed to have Muslim voters deleted and warned of protests, and that Congress leaders said the pre-printed forms found in Goshamahal and Bahadurpura were unsigned and were not accepted by booth officers.
items.quote: Following the Musheerabad incident, Congress leaders said they also found pre-printed forms seeking deletion of Muslim voters in Goshamahal and Bahadurpura constituencies, but these forms were unsigned and not accepted by the Booth Level Officers (BLOs).

items.headline: Contested Form 7s rejected, no bulk filings: Telangana DEO
items.claim: Siasat reported, citing PTI, that Hyderabad's District Election Officer R. V. Karnan said the Form 7s in Goshamahal and Musheerabad were not received in bulk and were rejected, the Goshamahal forms because they were unsigned and the Musheerabad ones because the electors were found living at the address.
items.quote: Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) Commissioner and District Election Officer R. V. Karnan told PTI that the Form 7 applications were not received in bulk but in much smaller numbers. In Goshamahal, the applicant did not sign the submitted forms, making them ineligible for consideration.
items.response: Siasat reported that BJP state president N. Ramchander Rao said no BJP booth agents had submitted any such Form 7 applications, and that the Chief Electoral Officer had said bulk forms from a party had to be properly enquired into and verified.

items.headline: Telangana SIR: Congress seeks SIT probe into alleged Form-7 misuse
items.claim: The News Minute quoted a memo of 5 October in which the Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, told District Election Officers that bulk Form 7 applications had been filed and that EROs should act under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act against anyone who knowingly made a false declaration.
items.quote: Meanwhile, the Telangana Chief Election Officer (CEO) C Sudharshan Reddy, on October 5, issued a notice stating, “[I]t has come to the notice of this office that there have been instances of filing of bulk applications in Form-7 before the EROs and it is also alleged that such forms are not genuine.”
items.response: Siasat reported that the CEO said this action would follow an inquiry. The memo itself was not found on the CEO Telangana website.

items.headline: SIR: Telangana CEO orders action over bulk Form 7 filings, Congress seeks SIT probe
items.claim: The South First reported that the Telangana Congress asked the Hyderabad Police Commissioner to register an FIR and set up a Special Investigation Team over pre-filled Form 7s in three constituencies, and to examine the BJP's role. These are the Congress's allegations.
items.quote: One such form seen by South First had the voter’s name and address pre-filled while the applicant’s details were blank. The Congress alleged that the forms had been printed in advance and asked the police to establish whether the persons named as applicants had actually signed them or even knew about the applications.
items.response: The South First reported that the Congress said the Police Commissioner had assured it he would study the matter and take action.

items.headline: Goshamahal Voter Deletion Row: Owaisi Seeks ECI Action
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that pre-printed Form 7s against 122 electors, all Muslim, were brought to booth 28 in Goshamahal by a BJP supporter, and that the booth officer refused them. This is AIMIM's allegation.
items.quote: We are placing a specific example before the Election Commission from Booth Number 28 in the Goshamahal assembly segment. As part of a deliberate plan, pre-printed Form 7 applications were submitted to delete the names of 122 electors.
items.response: Siasat reported the same day that the Telangana BJP had earlier rejected the allegations by the Congress and AIMIM that its workers submitted such forms.

items.headline: First FIR Related to Form-7
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Musheerabad ERO filed a police complaint, and Chikkadpally police registered a case, against a BJP booth agent who tried to submit 30 pre-printed Form 7s, the first such case in Telangana.
items.quote: The case was booked under BNS Sections 217 (giving false information to a public servant) and 318 (2) (cheating) and Section 31 of the Representation of People Act (making false declarations). “The BLO concerned and BLO supervisor collectively refused to receive the bulk forms in spite of repeated requests from the said BLA of BJP and have not given any acknowledgement in token of receipt…,” the FIR copy read.
items.response: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Congress welcomed the case and asked the police to find who printed and supplied the forms.

items.headline: Police probe fake Form-7 applications seeking deletion of 31 voters in Musheerabad
items.claim: Telangana Today reported that Chikkadpally police were checking the forms, signatures and voter details in the Musheerabad case and whether similar forms were filed elsewhere, and that the forms had reportedly been rejected.
items.quote: Police officials are verifying the forms, signatures, and voter details and are also looking into who prepared and submitted the applications and whether others were involved. Officials are also checking whether similar applications were filed elsewhere. Meanwhile, the disputed applications have reportedly been rejected following scrutiny.

items.headline: Enumeration Form 'Must' For Draft Electoral Roll
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported Hyderabad's District Election Officer R. V. Karnan explaining that booth officers would hand out enumeration forms already printed with each elector's details and photograph, which the elector completes and signs.
items.quote: The BLOs will carry forms already containing the elector’s photograph. Electors must paste a recent photograph, fill details and sign a declaration. BLOs will distribute forms with pre‑printed details of existing electors and guide households in filling them.

items.headline: BJP Lodges Complaint Against Officials Allegedly Favouring AIMIM
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Telangana BJP alleged to the Chief Electoral Officer that booth officers in Hyderabad were handing enumeration forms in bulk to AIMIM leaders at party camps and letting them upload filled forms. This is the BJP's allegation.
items.quote: The BJP on Tuesday alleged that booth level officers (BLOs) were avoiding mandatory house-to-house visits in the city. Instead, they were found to be distributing enumeration forms related to ongoing SIR exercise ‘in bulk’ to AIMIM leaders at party organised camps set up in several constituencies of the Hyderabad district, the BJP alleged.

items.headline: SIR: BJP Urges CEO To Conduct Probe Into Allegations
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that the BJP alleged that some booth officers in Serilingampally uploaded the blank back of enumeration forms to the Commission's app without the voter's details, and asked the Chief Electoral Officer for a probe. This is the BJP's allegation.
items.quote: Party’s State Election Commission Affairs committee chairman Marri Shashidhar Reddy alleged some BLOs have uploaded the reverse side of the Enumeration Form to the official BLO mobile application without filling in any mandatory voter details on the front side in Vivekananda Nagar division’s 575 to 580 booths.

items.headline: Form-7’s journey from a civic chore to a political weapon
items.claim: The Association for Democratic Reforms reported that Congress general secretary K. C. Venugopal wrote to the Commission on 29 January alleging misuse of Form 7 in several states, and that the Commission said there was no limit on forms per voter but that an ERO must verify when one person files more than five.
items.quote: In the wake of the swirling controversy over Form-7, the Election Commission has clarified that there is no limit on the number of forms a voter can submit in a constituency. However, in order to prevent misuse of the facility, if more than five objections are filed by an individual, the ERO will mandatorily verify the claims.
items.response: The same Commission clarification was reported by News On AIR on 17 January 2026.

items.headline: Form-7 flashpoint: Bengal sees clashes, rival claims of voter roll sabotage
items.claim: National Herald reported that Trinamool workers stopped a vehicle in Khatra, Bankura said to carry thousands of pre-filled Form 7s, that police seized it and began an inquiry, and that both parties traded allegations over bulk Form 7s on the last day for filing.
items.quote: The latest confrontations follow a flashpoint last week in Bankura’s Khatra subdivision, where TMC workers intercepted a vehicle said to be carrying thousands of pre-filled Form-7s. Police seized the vehicle and began an inquiry after TMC alleged the forms were intended to erase “legitimate voters” under cover of the SIR.
items.response: National Herald reported that the BJP alleged its workers were attacked and prevented from filing forms inside government offices.

items.headline: Form 7 controversy deepens strain on SIR 2.0
items.claim: National Herald reported that the Commission wrote to West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer to send all Form 7 objections to EROs by 16 February and dispose of them by statutory procedure, and that it had taken cognisance of reports of Form 7 records being burnt.
items.quote: The ECI's latest communication also cited reports alleging the burning of records related to Form 7 objections in parts of West Bengal — an issue it said it had taken cognisance of.

items.headline: In Assam, ‘forged’ forms aimed at deleting thousands of Muslim voters ring alarm bells
items.claim: Scroll reported that during Assam's Special Revision a booth officer in Karimganj North was handed objections against 133 voters on forms she described as half printed and half handwritten, and that hearings were suspended in three Nagaon constituencies after complaints of fake Form 7s.
items.quote: In several Muslim-majority districts and areas of Assam, bulk objections have been filed against voters, seeking to strike their names off the electoral roll. In Nagaon district, the hearing process has been suspended in three Assembly constituencies after complaints of fake Form 7 applications.
items.response: Scroll quoted a senior Commission official in Guwahati saying a voter can file any number of objections but that an ERO reviews them individually when one person files more than five.

items.headline: BJP workers in Assam say their names used to seek mass voter deletion – without their knowledge
items.claim: Scroll reported that at least seven people named as objectors on Form 7s in Assam, some of them BJP booth agents and members, said they had not filed the objections.
items.quote: Scroll found at least seven people who denied having filed the complaints, even when their names, voter identity cards and phone numbers had been used in the objection forms.
items.response: Scroll quoted BJP MP Kamakhya Prasad Tasa as saying anyone can file objections and that it is for the Election Commission to take a final call.

items.headline: ‘Nothing to hide’: Assam CM says he has told BJP members to file complaints against ‘Miya’ voters
items.claim: Scroll reported, citing The Indian Express, that Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said he had told BJP members to file Form 7s during the Special Revision.
items.quote: “There is nothing to hide about this,” he was quoted by the newspaper as saying. “I have held meetings, I have done video conferences, and I have told people that, wherever possible, they should fill Form 7s.

items.headline: Lakhs of ‘doubtful voters’ deleted in Assam based on BJP complaints, says Himanta Sarma
items.claim: Scroll reported, citing PTI, that after Assam's final roll the Chief Minister said several deletions had been made on complaints filed by BJP workers.
items.quote: “As far as possible, our party members filed complaints,” the BJP leader said. “Names have been struck off based on these.”

items.headline: Rajasthan SIR: BJP fraudulently removing Opposition supporters from voter lists, alleges Congress
items.claim: Scroll reported that Rajasthan Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra alleged that computer-printed Form 7s were distributed in every constituency and that booth agents' signatures were forged, and demanded a forensic inquiry. These are the Congress's allegations.
items.quote: “In every Assembly constituency, 10 thousand to 15 thousand fake computerised forms are printed,” he claimed. He added that several booth-level agents had given statements to the media that they had not signed these forms, and that the signatures were forged and the applications were incomplete.
items.response: Scroll reported that BJP minister Gautam Dak said a voter proposed for deletion gets time to be heard and that the Congress wanted to create a dispute.

items.headline: Muslim Voter Deletion Attempts in Alwar: EC's Silence Raises Questions
items.claim: The Quint reported that thousands of Form 7s in Alwar were filed in the names of BJP booth agents, several of whom said their signatures were forged, and that no FIR or inquiry had been announced a month later.
items.quote: As per copies of forms, seen by The Quint, they were overwhelmingly filed under the names of Booth Level Agents (BLAs) working for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and predominantly targeted Muslim voters in Rural Alwar. Yet no FIR, no administrative inquiry, no forensic audit of handwriting or digital origin has been announced in Alwar.
items.response: The Quint reported that calls to the District Magistrate and Sub-Divisional Magistrate for comment went unanswered.

items.headline: Inside the ‘organised’ attempt to delete 15,000 voters in Gujarat’s Somnath
items.claim: Newslaundry reported that 15,663 Form 7s in Somnath were filed by 269 people on forms with the voter's details printed and the objector's details handwritten, and that six named objectors filed affidavits saying they had not filed them.
items.quote: Of the 15,663 Form-7 applications, a staggering number appeared to be pre-filled and then submitted by just 269 people. Newslaundry has reviewed copies of Form-7s where voter details – such as name, mobile number, constituency, EPIC number, and booth number – are printed in English, while the objectors' details are handwritten in Gujarati.
items.response: Newslaundry reported that the District Election Officer, V. N. Upadhyay, said he had deployed six AEROs to verify the objections and assured that no name would be deleted arbitrarily.

items.headline: Gujarat HC notice: Probe sought into fake voter deletion pleas in SIR row
items.claim: Deccan Herald reported that the Gujarat High Court issued notice to the Commission and the state on two petitions seeking a Special Investigation Team inquiry into Form 7 objections filed during the SIR.
items.quote: The petitions have sought investigation by the Special Investigation Team. They have claimed that as part of a "larger conspiracy" thousands of illegal objection applications under form-7 were filed seeking deletion of voters' names during the recently concluded Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in the state.
items.response: Deccan Herald reported that the matter was posted for further hearing on 7 July.

items.headline: Fake Objections Filed To Delete Voter Names In Bhopal, Probe Ordered
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that Bhopal's Collector ordered a probe after a man named as objector on Form 7s in Bhopal South-West denied filing them, and that officials found incorrect or fake objector details in several of the district's 9,037 Form 7s.
items.quote: District officials said that across seven Assembly constituencies, a total of 9,037 objections have been filed through Form 7 under the SIR process. While the number is relatively small compared to the total electorate, several cases have been found to involve incorrect or fake complainant details, prompting further scrutiny.
items.response: ETV Bharat quoted District Election Officer Kaushlendra Vikram Singh saying no one's name would be deleted without verification.

items.headline: SIR: 544 Muslim voters marked for deletion in UP village leads to one man
items.claim: Siasat reported, citing The Indian Express, that Form 7s against 544 voters of a Shamli village were found with a booth officer, already printed with voters' EPIC numbers, and that the District Magistrate said the forms were fake and the probe found nothing.
items.quote: The forms were allegedly already printed with Electors’ Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers and other personal details. In the forms, the applicant cited relocation from the village as the reason for seeking their deletion from the electoral rolls.
items.response: DM Arvind Kumar Chauhan ordered a probe and later said that the case “didn’t have any substance.” “We got an investigation done and found nothing,” he added.

items.headline: Uttarakhand Congress alleges Form-7 misuse to delete voters during SIR, approaches EC
items.claim: The Pioneer reported that a Uttarakhand Congress delegation told the Chief Electoral Officer that one person had filed objections against about 6,400 voters and about 1,200 people had filed more than ten each. These are the Congress's figures.
items.quote: "Our data analysis revealed that a single individual has filed objections against the names of approximately 6,400 people. There are about 1,200 individuals who have submitted more than 10 objections each. An objection has even been filed against the name of a sitting Congress MLA," Rawat said.
items.response: The Pioneer reported that CEO V. V. R. C. Purushottam said the revision followed the rules and that observers had been sent to districts with many objections, and that Additional CEO Vijay Kumar Jogdande said an ERO must scrutinise cases where one person seeks the deletion of more than five names.

items.headline: Uttarakhand SIR: The unsolved mystery of BJP agents’ ‘forged’ objections against Muslim voters
items.claim: Newslaundry reported that 35 people named as objectors on 1,657 Form 7s in Jhabrera, 31 of them BJP booth agents, said in affidavits that their names, EPIC numbers and signatures had been misused.
items.quote: In affidavits submitted to the Haridwar district administration on August 18 and 19, each of the 35 said an “unknown person” used their name, EPIC number and a forged signature to file Form 7 applications – which are requests seeking the deletion of voters.
items.response: Newslaundry quoted Jhabrera ERO Devendra Singh Negi saying the objections were cancelled and the voters would not be deleted, and that the Election Commission would not order any investigation and those whose names were misused should file an FIR.

items.place: Delhi (Karol Bagh, Patel Nagar, Sangam Vihar)
items.headline: Delhi SIR: BJP Agent Files 35 Removal Requests in Two Days, ECINet Allows BLAs to Go Over 10-Claims Limit
items.claim: The Wire reported, citing The Hindu, that Form 10 lists for 21 to 27 September showed four people in Delhi filing more than ten Form 7s a day through the Commission's ECINET portal, which does not enforce the limit of ten a day for booth agents.
items.quote: The report also shows that booth-level agents (BLAs) bypassed the Election Commission’s cap on submitting only 10 applications a day during the claims and objections phase by filing through the panel’s ECINET portal, which has no such restriction in place. The ECINET software has no mechanism to impose the prescribed limit of 10.

items.headline: Five FIRs filed across Karnataka over alleged misuse of Form 7, BJP threatens protest
items.claim: The News Minute reported that five FIRs were registered in Belagavi, Bidar and Mysuru over Form 7s alleged to carry false information or forged signatures, and that in Belagavi the voters' details had been filled in beforehand with the objector's name handwritten or blank.
items.quote: The names and other details of voters had already been filled in, while the names of the persons shown as objectors were either handwritten or left blank. None of the five FIRs filed in connection with the Karnataka cases invokes the Representation of the People Act.
items.response: The News Minute reported that Karnataka CEO V. Anbu Kumar said that although 84,900 Form 7s had been received, no one had been taken off the rolls.

items.headline: Karnataka BJP leaders meet DGP, seek review of FIRs over Form 7 filings
items.claim: The News Minute reported that Karnataka BJP leaders asked the state police chief to review the FIRs against party workers, saying filing several Form 7s is not by itself a crime and the rules set no limit on their number.
items.quote: Ashoka said Congress leaders had pressured the police to register criminal cases against BJP workers. “Submitting Form 7 is not a crime. It is the Election Commission, not the police station, that has to determine the truth and validity of a voter,” he said.
items.response: The News Minute reported that Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara said ministers had gone to the CEO's office to submit a memorandum, not to stage a protest.

items.headline: Bihar Voter Roll Revision: Semi-Filled Forms Distributed to 87% Voters
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported the Commission saying that about 87 per cent of Bihar's 7.96 crore voters had been given semi-filled enumeration forms on the first booth officer visit.
items.quote: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Friday said that nearly 87 per cent of the 7.96 crore voters in Bihar had been provided with semi-filled enumeration forms for the ongoing special intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: Bihar SIR | BLOs Mass-Uploading Enumeration Forms Without Voters' Knowledge Or Consent : ADR Tells Supreme Court
items.claim: LiveLaw reported that the Association for Democratic Reforms told the Supreme Court that enumeration forms in Bihar were being uploaded by officials without voters' knowledge or consent. This is ADR's allegation in a court filing.
items.quote: "...enumeration forms are being mass-uploaded by BLOs without the knowledge or consent of the voters, in order to achieve the unrealistic target set by the ECI. Many voters have reported that their forms have been submitted online, despite never having met with any BLOs or signed any documents.
items.response: LiveLaw reported that ADR filed the rejoinder in reply to the Commission's counter-affidavit.

items.headline: 28 मतदाताओं के नाम हटाने के लिए फर्जी Form-7 का मामला, कोर्ट ने FIR के दिए आदेश
items.claim: A Judicial Magistrate First Class in Haldwani ordered the Banbhoolpura police on 6 October to register an FIR and investigate. A booth agent of a party had said that Form 7s seeking to delete 28 voters in part 134 were filed online in his name without his knowledge, and the court held that tracing who filed them needed a police investigation, Haldwani Express News reported.
items.quote: विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) प्रक्रिया के दौरान 28 मतदाताओं के नाम मतदाता सूची से हटाने के लिए कथित तौर पर फर्जी तरीके से Form-7 दाखिल किए जाने के मामले में न्यायिक मजिस्ट्रेट प्रथम, हल्द्वानी ने थाना बनभूलपुरा पुलिस को एफआईआर दर्ज कर विवेचना करने के निर्देश दिए हैं। ... हालांकि, अदालत ने स्पष्ट किया कि मतदाता सूची में संशोधन से संबंधित यह उपचार और कथित अपराध की पुलिस जांच दो अलग-अलग विषय हैं।
items.response: Haldwani Express News reported that the police had told the court the complaint concerned SIR Form 7s and that the complainant could object before the assistant returning officer.
items.note: City News Uttarakhand (9 Oct) carries nearly identical text, so both probably come from one note by the petitioner's lawyers; it is not an independent second report. No Amar Ujala, Dainik Jagran or Hindustan report was found (those sites are not reachable by this agent's search). Both name the complainant, a BLA-2 of ward 31, Indranagar; the draft does not. The Form 7s were filed on 12 August 2026; police complaint 24 August; BNSS 175(3) application 15 September.

items.headline: SIR: Single Jharkhand Assembly Constituency Accounts for Over a Third of Voter Deletion Requests
items.claim: Of 13,443 Form 7 applications for deletion in Jharkhand, 4,790 came from the Chatra Assembly seat, about 36% of the state's total, in figures the Chief Electoral Officer released on 1 October, The Wire reported, citing the Hindustan Times. West Singhbhum had 1,906 and Deoghar 1,099.
items.quote: About one in every three requests to remove names from Jharkhand's electoral roll has come from just one assembly constituency, data released on Thursday (October 1) by the state's chief electoral officer (CEO) revealed. ... Of the 13,443 Form 7 submitted for deletion of names, 4,790 pertain to the Chatra assembly seat in Chatra district, roughly 36% of the state's total.
items.response: The Wire reported that the Chief Electoral Officer said the Chatra figures were checked with the district administration and no bulk applications beyond the limit were found, and that address changes on Form 8 generate Form 7 entries automatically.
items.note: Date is The Wire's (published 2 Oct 2026, 4:23 PM). The CEO released the figures on Thursday 1 October, as the claim says.

items.headline: 91,278 Form 7 applications received in Karnataka, officials says no names deleted so far
items.claim: Karnataka's Chief Electoral Officer said 91,278 Form 7 applications were received between 16 June and 4 October, that no name had yet been deleted because of one, and that each would go through a notice and hearing before an officer decided. He said EROs would inquire into bulk applications and that his office had registered no FIR, The News Minute reported.
items.quote: Karnataka has received 91,278 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names from electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR). However, no voter has been deleted through the process so far. ... “Just because objections have been filed, no name has been deleted so far from the electoral roll,” Anbukkumar said at a press conference.
items.note: ETV Bharat (5 Oct) agrees on 91,278 (16 June to 4 October), 58,220 by 23 September, no deletion yet on a Form 7, and EROs to inquire into bulk applications; it adds that bulk applications were filed in Babaleshwar and some were later withdrawn. TNM gives the district leaders (Bidar 5,953, Shivamogga 5,936, Dakshina Kannada 5,534).

items.headline: NDA leaders seek K'taka Guv intervention over 'govt interference' in SIR
items.claim: A BJP and JD(S) delegation including Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy and R Ashoka asked Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot to direct the state government to stop registering criminal cases against people who filed Form 7 objections, ThePrint reported, carrying PTI. They alleged police were being misused to intimidate BJP workers and that the Chief Electoral Office had given in to the state government.
items.quote: It urged Gehlot to issue appropriate directions to the state government to ensure that "false and unwarranted" FIRs and criminal cases under the BNS are not registered against individuals, including BJP workers, in connection with the SIR exercise.
items.response: No response from the state government, the Chief Electoral Officer or Congress was reported.
items.note: The delegation met CEO V Anbukkumar on 5 October. Its letter named FIRs in Bhalki, Market Area (Belagavi), Vyalikaval (Bengaluru), Ballari and Narasimharaja (Mysuru).

items.headline: K'taka: BJP-JDS delegation seeks withdrawal of FIR over Form-7 issue
items.claim: A BJP and JD(S) delegation led by Jayanagar MLA C K Ramamurthy went to Jayanagar police station in Bengaluru and demanded that the FIR against BJP workers over Form 7 applications be withdrawn, IANS reported. They warned of an intensified agitation if it was not, and alleged that applications meant to be confidential had been handed to Congress workers.
items.quote: The delegation demanded that the FIR be withdrawn immediately.
items.response: No police response was reported.

items.headline: K'taka: BJP-JDS delegation seeks withdrawal of FIR over Form-7 issue
items.claim: Police at Shanivarasanthe in Kodagu district registered a case against five BJP booth level workers on a complaint that they sought the deletion of 64 voters in Byadagutta village through Form 7 applications, IANS reported.
items.quote: Police have registered a case against the five persons and are investigating the allegations.
items.note: Date of the FIR not given; the date is the publication date. The page says Madikeri district, whose headquarters it is; the district is Kodagu. The complainant and the accused are private persons and are not named.

items.headline: Karnataka SIR Row: FIR Against BJP BLAs For 'Fake Voter Deletion' In Jayanagar
items.claim: Jayanagar police in Bengaluru registered an FIR against two BJP booth level agents on a complaint by Karnataka Mahila Congress president Sowmya Reddy, alleging Form 7 applications with forged signatures to delete 5,698 voters by falsely claiming they had shifted.
items.response: No response from the BJP, the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission was reported.
items.note: FIR registered on the night of 5 October; its period is 16 June to 5 October. The booth agents and two residents are named on the page and are left out.

items.headline: Congress and BJP-JD(S) trade charges over bulk Form 7 filings during SIR in Karnataka
items.claim: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar alleged on 6 October that BJP and JD(S) workers took back more than a lakh Form 7 applications they had filed in bulk.
items.quote: "They have burnt them."
items.response: BJP MLC C T Ravi asked the Commission to register a case against people making baseless allegations.

items.headline: Karnataka BJP Leader Withdraws Form-7 Pleas To Delete 243 Voters After SIR Row
items.claim: A BJP leader in Koppa, Chikkamagaluru, wrote on 1 October to withdraw Form 7 objections seeking the deletion of 243 voters filed on 21 and 22 September, saying the voters were found on re-verification to live within the polling stations' areas, Free Press Journal reported.
items.quote: "withdrawing the Form-7 objections submitted on September 21 and 22"
items.response: No response from the election authorities was reported.
items.note: The article describes the five who filed as BJP taluk leaders. None is named here. The religion of the 243 voters is reported as an allegation and is left out.

items.headline: Delhi CEO restricts number of Form 7 an individual can file to raise objections
items.claim: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer capped Form 7 objections at ten per voter for the whole claims and objections period, and five a month during continuous updation, citing bulk objections on unsubstantiated grounds.
items.quote: A maximum number of 10 Form-7 applications during the entire period of claims and objections
items.note: The Commission's order itself was not opened. Also carried by The Hawk. The page does not say whether the limit applies outside Delhi.

items.headline: For Every Form 6 Disposal, Six Form 7s Cleared in Delhi: Report
items.claim: The Wire reported, citing The Hindu's analysis of Delhi's constituency data, that 569 Form 6 applications and 3,209 Form 7 applications were disposed of between 31 August and 4 October, about six Form 7s for every Form 6. It said 2,352 of the Form 7s were disposed of in the last two weeks, and that 2.12 lakh Form 6 and 51,747 Form 7 applications had been submitted from 16 June, before the claims period began on 31 August.
items.quote: only 569 Form 6 applications were disposed of between August 31 and October 4
items.response: No response from the Chief Electoral Officer was reported. On 22 October the Chief Electoral Officer's office replaced the weekly disposal report on which this analysis rests, and officials said the earlier figures were wrong. The revised figures are entered separately, from The Hindu of 23 October.
items.note: One item for two reprints of The Hindu's analysis: The Wire and Madhyamam Online (7 Oct). The Hindu's original was not opened. Neither page says whether the data came from the CEO.

items.headline: Over 24,000 Form 7 Applications Received During SIR In Telangana
items.claim: The Chief Electoral Officer's data for the claims and objections period to 7 October showed 24,323 Form 7 applications in Telangana and 12,204 names deleted, PTI reported.
items.response: State BJP president N Ramchander Rao said the Commission decides deletions only after field inquiries.
items.note: Also in Deccan Chronicle (8 Oct), Telangana Today (8 Oct) and The Hans India (9 Oct). Goshamahal shows 222 received and 242 removed, as printed. The 1 October figure of 28,753 is form7-02.

items.case: W.P. No. 31887 of 2026 and W.P. No. 31893 of 2026, two BJP booth agents' petitions, Karnataka High Court
items.headline: SIR: Karnataka High Court grants relief to BJP booth agents booked for attempting to delete voters
items.claim: The Karnataka High Court stayed two FIRs against two BJP booth agents accused of filing bulk Form 7s against voters in Bengaluru's Malleshwaram constituency. The judge said the FIRs looked premature because the registration officer had not yet decided the Form 7s.
items.quote: The concerned officer will decide.
items.response: The State said the allegations of impersonation and forgery needed investigation and that the agents filed more applications than allowed. The complainant's counsel said the bulk filing was a conspiracy aimed at OBC and SC/ST voters.
items.note: Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde, Friday 9 October; next hearing 27 October 2026. The Vyalikaval FIR concerns 778 voters in Ward 64 and the Yeshwanthapura FIR 136 voters in Ward 45. The petitioners are named in the case titles and are given by role here.

items.case: CRL.P 102783/2026 and connected matters, a BJP functionary's petition, Karnataka High Court at Dharwad
items.headline: Karnataka High Court Grants Interim Protection To BJP Leader Booked Over Alleged Attempt To Delete Muslim Voters' Names During SIR
items.claim: The Karnataka High Court at Dharwad told the police to take no coercive steps until 13 October against a BJP functionary and two supporters, booked over Form 7s against voters in Belagavi. Police allege about 198 fabricated Form 7s were handed to the booth officer. On 13 October Justice Venkatesh Naik T stayed the investigation until the next hearing, citing a coordinate bench's stay in similar cases on 9 October, Bar and Bench reported. The Court allowed the State to seek to have the order modified or vacated, and posted the matter for 29 October.
items.quote: Till then, the respondent-police/IO shall not take any coercive steps against the petitioners.
items.response: The Government Pleader sought time to file objections and the latest investigation report.
items.note: Justice Venkatesh Naik T. Next hearing 13 October 2026. Continues the Belagavi FIR in form7-32. Hearing date not given; the date is the publication date. The petitioner is named by role. The stay: Bar and Bench, by Siddesh M S, published 14 October 2026, 8:48 am IST (modified 15 October), read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026. It reports the order of Tuesday 13 October and says the protection of 8 October came from 'another bench', where the note above has Justice Venkatesh Naik T for both. The two are not reconciled here.

items.headline: Delhi SIR: revised data show sharp increase in Form 6 disposal rate
items.claim: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer replaced the weekly report of applications disposed of on 22 October, and officials told The Hindu that the figures published until then were wrong. The revised report shows 1,07,451 of 4,59,796 Form 6 applications for inclusion and 47,105 of 67,709 Form 7 applications disposed of from 31 August to 18 October, about 23% and 70%. The earlier report had shown 1,238 Form 6 disposals to 11 October. Tri Nagar is the only constituency with no Form 6 disposal recorded in any of the seven weeks.
items.quote: The weekly data being uploaded till now was wrong and it was not reflecting the disposals that happened since August 31, we noticed after the newspaper report,
items.response: The Hindu attributes the quoted explanation to an unnamed official and does not say which office the official works in. More than 3.5 lakh Form 6 applications were still to be disposed of. Claims close on 30 October, every application is to be disposed of by 30 November, and the final roll is due on 4 December.
items.note: By Suruchi Kumari, published 23 October 2026, 1:04 am IST, read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 23 October 2026. The disposals include applications received before the draft roll of 31 August.

items.headline: Tracking ECI’s U-Turns on Form 7: In West Bengal, After Allowing Unlimited Objections, ECI Caps Them at 10
items.claim: The Wire reported that on 16 January 2026, during West Bengal's extended claims period, the Commission told the state's Chief Electoral Officer in writing that the law set no limit on the number of Form 7 objections one voter could file, and that on 9 October it capped them at ten per voter for a whole claims period, in an instruction to every state. The October instruction cites a paragraph of the Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2023 against entertaining objections presented in bulk by an individual, which the January letter did not mention. Reading the Chief Electoral Officer's daily bulletins, the report counts 3,143 objections from party agents by 20 January, 2,926 from BJP agents and 217 from Trinamool agents, and finds that 2,539 of them first appear in the bulletin dated the day after the extended window closed on 19 January.
items.quote: Currently, there are no such restrictions on number of Form 7 to be filled/submitted by an elector of that constituency to ERO/AERO as per law,
items.response: The report says the Commission has not said whether objections filed in January will be looked at again.
items.note: By Aparna Bhattacharya, posted 22 October 2026, 6:38 pm IST, read in full on 23 October 2026 from The Wire's content API with curl. The quote is from the Commission's letter of 16 January as the report prints it. The report names private persons who received notices, and they are not named here. The report notes the late entries may have been received by 19 January and entered late.

items.headline: Nearly One-Third of Form 7 Objections in Delhi SIR Seeking Voter Deletions Not Disclosed Publicly: Report
items.claim: The Wire reported, citing The Hindu, that 4,263 of the 13,462 Form 7 applications Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer received between 31 August and 16 October, or 31.67%, had not been published in the Form 10 lists. The Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2023 requires each objection to be listed publicly for seven days before an Electoral Registration Officer can act on it.
items.quote: Essentially, if any objection has not been publicly listed, then it is invalid and cannot be acted upon. Processing such an application will be a violation of rules,
items.response: The Hindu reported that it sent questions to the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office and had no response by the time of publication.
items.note: The Wire Staff, posted 22 October 2026, 12:11 pm IST, read in full on 23 October 2026 from The Wire's content API with curl. The quote is a senior election official's, as The Hindu reported it. The Hindu's own report was not found in its news sitemap and was not opened.

items.headline: Karnataka SIR: Form 7 submissions surged from 58,475 to 2.28 lakh in 1 month, shows data
items.claim: Karnataka received 2,28,917 Form 7 applications between 16 June and 22 October, 1,70,442 of them after 23 September, when the count stood at 58,475, The Indian Express reported from official data. The Chief Electoral Officer's office said every Form 7 received up to 23 September had been cleared on priority and that hearings for all 43.82 lakh voters sent notices were over. Bangalore Urban had the most submissions in the paper's table, 24,268. The ruling Congress has alleged that the BJP is misusing Form 7 to file objections in bulk.
items.quote: All Form-7 applications received up to September 23 have been cleared on priority, the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer office said in a statement issued on Friday.
items.response: After a Congress protest at the Chief Electoral Officer's office earlier this month, the Chief Electoral Officer directed Electoral Registration Officers to look into the allegations. The state BJP has rejected them. The final roll is due on 27 October.
items.note: Express News Service, published 24 October 2026, 3:39 am IST, read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026. The online text cuts off at 'Most objections from' and then gives a table of four districts. The Hindu of 24 October and the Chief Electoral Officer's note of 24 August both give 23 September as the last date for claims and objections, and The Hindu says Form 6 applications filed after it will not be reflected in the final roll. Neither says how Form 7s filed after that date will be handled. The paper's figures for the roll (5.54 crore before, 4.46 crore in the draft) match the site's Karnataka data (5,54,32,314 and 4,46,35,975). Its 'over 1.08 crore' left out is a little above the site's 1,07,96,339.
